title: Passing value on through honest foundations

captions.physics: Openly dismantling an unsound external arrangement
captions.energy: Seeking truthful foundations beyond convincing appearances
captions.emotions: Connection with a meaningfully shared inheritance

meaning: Truthful shared foundations can inspire you when revising an external form preserves living connection with value passed on to people.
text: The two Towers occupy different positions here: action and the foundation for which action is taken. The Tower in the physical position of Sahasrara describes openly dismantling an unsound arrangement. The Tower in energy supports a constructive wish for truthful foundations rather than maintaining persuasive appearances. The Hierophant in emotions brings connection with value meaningfully passed on. You enjoy belonging to an inheritance people can understand and continue, without requiring them to accept an attractive external form as sufficient confirmation of everything being claimed about its history or significance.

You help prepare an account of an old city tradition together. Its dramatic central episode proves a recent addition unsupported by sources. You remove it from the main display, retaining actual evidence and separately identifying the later retelling. **Value travels more securely when its foundations withstand honest revision.** A visitor recognises a familiar custom in a less ceremonial but understandable account. You feel connected with living memory that needs no invented grandeur to have meaning.

The difficulty may arise if exposing one episode becomes the entire exhibition’s centre. Honest motivation and connection with value remain supportive, but action eclipses confirmed material. Practice benefits from giving that content its own place. Revision then frees transmission from false support without making the whole endeavour exclusively a story about the mistake dismantled.
